correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication gives exactly three active generators. The component union follows from a complete two-case split on x; the stronger ideal identity is proved by explicit monomial ideal intersections and primeness of the fourth binomial prime, so the original scheme is reduced over all fields. Dimensions and rationality follow from prime ideals, and the active-coordinate finite-field partition proves the q-polynomial. Independent exact enumeration in four finite fields and Groebner checks in four characteristics corroborate the proof; finite checks are not relied on for generality.

value.rationale: The object is a natural one-sided complex constrained by a fixed complete flag. The n=4 case is the first threshold of failure of equidimensionality (n=2 is affine; n=3 has two equal-dimensional components). A complete prime decomposition, geometric reducedness and the exact q-point polynomial at this threshold are structurally motivated; no arbitrary slice or tiny numerical improvement is the central claim.
